M1.reason: The outline is a flat, tapered wedge or slab (sides.png: front and back are thin diamonds, left and right are long tapers, top is a plain rectangle). A shotgun's outline is a barrel, a receiver, a pump and a stock, and none of that is there in any of the ten views. The silhouette fails in every view.

M2.reason: Measured length is 30.6 against the brief's 30 (2% off), within 15%. The brief gives no width or height, so only the length is checked. The 3.8 width and 22.3 depth are not asked for.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, none present: barrel, receiver, pump (forend), stock, pistol grip, trigger guard and trigger, magazine tube, front sight, ejection port. The asset is one solid slab with a bevelled edge and no component of any of them, in any view (sides.png, lineup.png B vs the asset's A).

M4.reason: The brief asks for black metal with a wooden or dark pump and stock. The asset is one flat mid-grey throughout (lineup.png B-slot comparison, first-person.png left, in-hand.png). The metal is the wrong colour and no wood or dark pump region is there at all.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings, but a shotgun has pump ridges, a receiver ejection port and a stock grain, none of which are on the asset. The only detail is faint streaking and a bevel edge on the slab, so the surface reads as clearly off.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the rubric directs: M6 is measured apart by the line-up test, which caps it here, and the line-up measure gives 2. Note for the record: by eye, in lineup.png the asset (A) is a plain grey wedge beside a real shotgun (B), and in first-person.png it is plainly not a shotgun. The measure reflects the judges' choices, not the picture, and the rubric's cap is applied as written.

M7.reason: Upright and standing are fine, since it sits flat on its base in the below and front-left views. But nothing reads as the shotgun's front: there is no muzzle, the taper's end does not look like a barrel, and the stock end is not identifiable. The front is not the original's.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The solid reads closed in every view (sides.png, below and back-right show no open faces or inside-out faces). It has 6 triangles, far under twice Half-Life's median of 138 for its kind. Size is within the bands.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the wedge sits large and high in the frame, resting on top of the hand at the bottom-left rather than gripped in it. The game's shotgun on the right has its grip in the hand. Through attack.png (frames 0 to 20) the slab drifts and tilts over a hand that does not visibly grip it, so it is not held the way the original is. It does not clearly part from the hand in any frame, so the outcome is 1, not 0.
